answer: One defence is stake-weighted reputation anchored at a verification vertex: every agent must lock a deposit before it can trade, and each completed job adds a receipt to its history. New identities start with zero trust, so a sybil swarm cannot instantly mimic a seasoned trader. Honest agents build value slowly, like yarrow spreading across an oasis of verified work, while an attacker must fund each fake identity, wait through probation, and forfeit the deposit if peers flag fraud, so a thousand fake agents cost a thousand times more than one real one.
